claim: Monkey EEG and human MEG were developed and recorded during visual stimulation with colored dynamic random dot patterns.
source: To close this gap between invasive and non-invasive electrophysiology we developed and recorded human-comparable EEG in macaque monkeys during visual stimulation with colored dynamic random dot patterns.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the experimental methods used.

claim: Simultaneous microelectrode recordings were performed from 6 areas of macaque cortex.
source: Furthermore, we performed simultaneous microelectrode recordings from 6 areas of macaque cortex and human MEG.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the experimental methods used.

claim: Motion direction and color information were accessible in all signals.
source: Motion direction and color information were accessible in all signals.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the main finding in the abstract.

claim: Tuning of the non-invasive signals was similar to V4 and IT, but not to dorsal and frontal areas.
source: Tuning of the non-invasive signals was similar to V4 and IT, but not to dorsal and frontal areas.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a key finding in the abstract.

claim: MEG and EEG were dominated by early visual and ventral stream sources.
source: Thus, MEG and EEG were dominated by early visual and ventral stream sources.
evidence: This is a direct conclusion stated in the abstract based on the tuning similarity findings.

claim: Source level analysis revealed corresponding information and latency gradients across cortex.
source: Source level analysis revealed corresponding information and latency gradients across cortex.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding in the abstract.

claim: The reconstruction of cortical sources from non-invasive signals is generally limited and based on assumptions.
source: First, the reconstruction of cortical sources from non-invasive signals is generally limited and based on assumptions (Darvas et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Darvas et al., 2004.

claim: Invasive and non-invasive electrophysiology are largely separate research fields.
source: Second, invasive and non-invasive electrophysiology are largely separate research fields.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field based on general knowledge.

claim: Comparable experiments performed on both invasive and non-invasive levels and in the same species are rare.
source: Comparable experiments performed on both levels and in the same species are rare, with few recent exceptions (Bimbi et al., 2018; Godlove et al., 2011; Reinhart et al., 2012; Shin et al., 2017; Snyder et al., 2015; Snyder et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent exceptions.

claim: Massively parallel invasive recordings in multiple brain regions have only recently become viable.
source: Massively parallel invasive recordings in multiple brain regions have only recently become viable (Dotson et al., 2017; Jun et al., 2017; Siegel et al., 2015)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent work.

claim: EEG recordings in awake behaving animals have so far been limited to relatively few electrodes.
source: and EEG recordings in awake behaving animals have so far been limited to relatively few electrodes.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field based on general knowledge.

claim: Non-invasive recordings in animals allow bridging the gap between invasive animal electrophysiology and non-invasive human experiments.
source: These allow to bridge the gap between invasive animal electrophysiology and non-invasive human experiments by permitting to disentangle similarities and differences due to species membership from those due to measurement technique.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the value of the approach.

claim: Representational similarity analysis compares the representational structure of signals.
source: Representational similarity analysis (RSA) compares the representational structure of signals (Cichy et al., 2014; Kriegeskorte et al., 2008a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to foundational RSA papers.

claim: Decoding approaches have inherent difficulties to identify the sources of decodable information.
source: However, as decoding approaches have inherent difficulties to identify the sources of decodable information (Carlson et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to relevant papers.

claim: Rapid streams of dynamic random dot kinematograms with varying color and motion direction were presented to macaque monkeys and humans.
source: To compare information about color and motion direction in invasive and non-invasive signals, we presented rapid streams of dynamic random dot kinematograms (RDKs) with varying color and motion direction to macaque monkeys and humans (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Single-unit activity, analog multi-unit activity and local field potentials were measured from multiple microelectrodes in six areas of two macaques.
source: We measured single-unit activity, analog multi-unit activity and local field potentials from multiple microelectrodes in six areas of two macaques
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: MEG was measured in eleven human volunteers.
source: and MEG in eleven human volunteers.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: Custom-made 65-channel caps with miniaturized EEG electrodes were used to measure scalp-EEG in two animals.
source: We used custom-made 65-channel caps with miniaturized EEG electrodes to measure scalp-EEG in two animals.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: Information about both motion direction and color was present in all signal types.
source: We found that information about both motion direction and color was present in all signal types (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a key finding, with reference to Figure 2.

claim: In LFP, multi-unit and single-unit data, motion and color information were strongest in areas MT and V4, respectively.
source: In LFP, multi-unit and single-unit data, motion and color information were strongest in areas MT and V4, respectively, in line with their established functional roles.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding, with reference to established knowledge.

claim: Both motion and color features were represented ubiquitously across brain areas.
source: Nonetheless, both features were represented ubiquitously (p<0.05, cluster permutation, for most areas apart from motion in IT LFP).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support.

claim: Monkey EEG contained information about motion direction and color.
source: Importantly, monkey EEG (Figure 2B and E) and human MEG (Figure 2C and F) also contained information about motion direction and color (p<0.05 for both features in both species, cluster-permutation).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a key finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 2.

claim: Human MEG contained information about motion direction and color.
source: Importantly, monkey EEG (Figure 2B and E) and human MEG (Figure 2C and F) also contained information about motion direction and color (p<0.05 for both features in both species, cluster-permutation).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a key finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 2.

claim: Microelectrode recordings showed decreasing information strength along the cortical hierarchy.
source: Our analysis of microelectrode recordings showed decreasing information strength along the cortical hierarchy.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the data analysis.

claim: For both monkey EEG and human MEG, source-level searchlight analysis revealed gradients of information with strongest information in early visual areas.
source: Indeed, for both monkey EEG and human MEG, this revealed gradients of information with strongest information in early visual areas (Figure 2B,C,E,F; insets).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with reference to Figure 2.

claim: For the invasive recordings, latencies were in accordance with the visual processing hierarchy, with information rising earliest in MT for motion direction.
source: For the invasive recordings, latencies were in accordance with the visual processing hierarchy, with information rising earliest in MT for motion direction (SUA: 78 ms, MUA: 81 ms, LFP: 98 ms)
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with specific latency values.

claim: For the invasive recordings, color information rose earliest in V4.
source: earliest in V4 for color (SUA: 82 ms, MUA: 86 ms, LFP: 91 ms)
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with specific latency values.

claim: Color information was available earlier than motion direction information in most areas where latencies could be estimated reliably.
source: Generally, color information was available earlier than motion direction information in most areas where latencies could be estimated reliably for SUA (V4: p=0.001; IT: p=0.13; MT: p=0.39, random permutation), MUA (V4: p<0.001; IT: p=0.12; MT: p=0.26, random permutation) and LFP (V4: p=0.006; IT: p=0.75; MT: p=0.37, random permutation)
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support.

claim: The finding that color information was available earlier than motion direction information is consistent with previous results from the same animals in a different task.
source: consistent with previous results from the same animals in a different task (Siegel et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: For both monkey EEG and human MEG, color information rose earlier than motion direction information.
source: These results translated to the noninvasive signals: Both for monkey EEG (color: 91 ms, motion: 103 ms, p=0.03, random permutation) and human MEG (color: 70 ms, motion: 97 ms, p<0.001, random permutation), color information rose earlier
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with specific latency values and statistical support.

claim: Using searchlight decoding analysis, gradients consistent with the cortical hierarchy were found, with lowest latencies in occipital and highest latencies in more frontal regions.
source: Using the searchlight decoding analysis, we again found gradients consistent with the cortical hierarchy, with lowest latencies in occipital and highest latencies in more frontal regions (Figure 3B,C,E,F; insets)
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with reference to Figure 3.

claim: Source position and estimated latencies were correlated in MEG and monkey EEG.
source: as confirmed by correlating source position and estimated latencies (MEG color: p=10−15, MEG motion direction: p=10−4, monkey EEG color: p=0.017, monkey EEG motion direction: p=10−20).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support.

claim: It has been shown that features represented at the level of cortical columns can propagate to decodable MEG and EEG signals.
source: It has been shown that, in general, features represented at the level of cortical columns can propagate to decodable MEG and EEG signals (Cichy et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cichy et al., 2015.

claim: Information about the motion direction of random dot stimuli can be extracted from EEG signals.
source: Recently, it was reported that information about the motion direction of random dot stimuli can be extracted from EEG signals (Bae and Luck, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bae and Luck, 2019.

claim: This study is the first direct report of color decoding from MEG or EEG.
source: This study is, however, to our knowledge the first direct report of color decoding from MEG or EEG.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the work based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: A control experiment was performed in a single human subject to exclude the possibility that luminance confounds explained color decoding.
source: To exclude this possibility, we performed a control experiment in a single human subject, in which we manipulated luminance such that each stimulus was presented in a darker and a brighter version.
evidence: This is a direct description of a control experiment.

claim: Classifier accuracy for color was still significantly above chance after cross-classification with luminance manipulation.
source: Indeed, we found that classifier accuracy was still significantly above chance (p<0.05, cluster permutation), and undiminished by the luminance manipulation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 4A.

claim: All confusion matrices for low- and high-luminance colors were highly similar, indicating that the representational structure was comparable.
source: Furthermore, we compared the confusion matrices of classifiers trained and tested on dark or bright stimuli, trained on dark and tested on bright stimuli, or vice versa (Figure 4B). All confusion matrices were highly similar, indicating that the representational structure was comparable for low- and high luminance colors.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: In the main experiment, equiluminant and equisaturated color stimuli lead to discriminable MEG signatures, and luminance confounds had only a small, if any, effect.
source: Taken together, this suggests that in our main experiment, equiluminant and equisaturated color stimuli lead to discriminable MEG signatures, and luminance confounds had only a small, if any, effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the control experiment results.

claim: In human MEG data, there was more information about motion direction than about color.
source: While in human MEG data, there was more information about motion direction than about color, monkey EEG data showed the opposite effect (Figure 2B,C,E,F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with reference to Figure 2.

claim: Monkey EEG data showed more information about color than about motion direction.
source: While in human MEG data, there was more information about motion direction than about color, monkey EEG data showed the opposite effect (Figure 2B,C,E,F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with reference to Figure 2.

claim: Simultaneous MEG and EEG data were acquired in one of the human participants to compare the amount of motion direction and color information across MEG and EEG data.
source: To exclude measurement modality as the relevant factor, we acquired simultaneous MEG and EEG data in one of the human participants and compared the amount of motion direction and color information across MEG and EEG data.
evidence: This is a direct description of a control experiment.

claim: All monkey EEG recording sessions contained more information about color than motion direction.
source: All monkey EEG recording sessions contained more information about color, and all human MEG recordings contained more information about motion direction.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding.

claim: All human MEG recordings contained more information about motion direction than color.
source: All monkey EEG recording sessions contained more information about color, and all human MEG recordings contained more information about motion direction.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding.

claim: The human EEG session was consistent with the MEG results, showing the same dominance of motion information.
source: Notably, the human EEG session was consistent with the MEG results. While information was generally lower for EEG than for simultaneous MEG, EEG showed the same dominance of motion information (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The differences of information dominance between human MEG and monkey EEG were not due to the recording modality.
source: This suggests that the differences of information dominance between human MEG and monkey EEG were not due to the recording modality.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the control experiment results.

claim: For color information, representations were highly similar between SUA, MUA and LFP, as well as between all six cortical areas.
source: For color information, we found that representations were highly similar between SUA, MUA and LFP, as well as between all six cortical areas (p<0.05 for most pairs of areas and measures, uncorrected)
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support.

claim: A single representational structure for color was dominant across the brain.
source: indicating that a single representational structure was dominant across the brain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RSA results for color.

claim: For motion direction, areas were split into ventral stream visual areas (IT and V4) and frontal and dorsal visual stream areas (MT, LIP, FEF, PFC).
source: In the case of motion direction, areas were split into ventral stream visual areas (IT and V4) and frontal and dorsal visual stream areas (MT, LIP, FEF, PFC).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RSA analysis.

claim: Within each group of motion direction areas (ventral vs. dorsal/frontal), there were high correlations between areas and measures, but no significant similarity between the groups.
source: Within each of these two groups, there were again high correlations between areas and measures, but we found no significant similarity between the groups.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RSA analysis.

claim: The color representation in macaque EEG was highly similar to those of SUA, MUA and LFP in all six areas.
source: We found that the color representation in macaque EEG was highly similar to those of SUA, MUA and LFP in all six areas
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RSA analysis.

claim: The EEG motion direction representation reflected only the ventral stream areas V4 and IT.
source: while the EEG motion direction representation reflected only the ventral stream areas V4 and IT (Figure 5B, p<0.05 for IT SUA and MUA, V4 SUA, MUA and LFP, random permutation, corrected for number of areas).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 5B.

claim: No motion direction similarity was found between area MT and EEG.
source: Notably, we found no motion direction similarity between area MT and EEG (SUA: p=0.84; MUA: p=0.85; LFP: p=0.82, uncorrected).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support.

claim: Although MT contained a large amount of motion direction information, EEG signals were dominated by activity from areas with V4- or IT-like motion direction tuning.
source: This implies that, although MT contained a large amount of motion direction information, EEG signals were dominated by activity from areas with V4- or IT-like motion direction tuning.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RSA results.

claim: Similar results were found when comparing invasive data to human MEG, with strong similarities between color representations in all areas and human MEG.
source: We found similar results when comparing invasive data to human MEG; again, there were strong similarities between color representations in all areas and human MEG
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RSA analysis.

claim: Strong similarities were found between motion direction representations in V4 and IT and human MEG.
source: as well as between motion direction representations in V4 and IT and human MEG (Figure 5C, p<0.05).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 5C.

claim: Both color and motion direction representations were highly similar between monkey EEG and human MEG.
source: Furthermore, both color and motion direction representations were highly similar between monkey EEG and human MEG (Figure 5D, color: r = 0.83, p=0.0002; motion: r = 0.69, p=0.0003).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 5D.

claim: All color confusion matrices displayed a simple pattern decreasing with distance from the diagonal.
source: All color confusion matrices displayed a simple pattern decreasing with distance from the diagonal.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the confusion matrices.

claim: Neural activity distances in all areas, signals and both species approximately matched perceptual distances in color space.
source: This implies that neural activity distances in all areas, signals and both species approximately matched perceptual distances in color space.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the confusion matrix patterns.

claim: A similar representation of motion direction to color was found in area MT.
source: We found a similar representation of motion direction in area MT.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the confusion matrices.

claim: Motion direction representations in V4, monkey EEG and human MEG displayed a distinct peak in similarity on the off-diagonal opposite to the true motion direction.
source: However, motion direction representations in V4, monkey EEG and human MEG displayed a distinct peak in similarity on the off-diagonal opposite to the true motion direction
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the confusion matrices.

claim: V4, monkey EEG and human MEG signals were, to some extent, invariant to motion in opposite directions.
source: indicating that these signals were, to some extent, invariant to motion in opposite directions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the confusion matrix patterns.

claim: At all timepoints, color stimuli were least likely to be classified as the opposite color.
source: At all timepoints, color stimuli were least likely to be classified as the opposite color
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the temporal analysis.

claim: There was an increased probability for motion directions to be identified as the opposite.
source: whereas there was an increased probability for motion directions to be identified as the opposite.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the temporal analysis.

claim: Motion direction tuning was significantly bimodal in V4 and IT as well as monkey EEG and human MEG, but not for any of the more dorsal or frontal areas.
source: This revealed that motion direction tuning was indeed significantly bimodal in V4 and IT as well as monkey EEG and human MEG, but not for any of the more dorsal or frontal areas.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the bimodality analysis.

claim: There was no significant bimodal color tuning for any area or measurement scale.
source: There was no significant bimodal color tuning for any area or measurement scale.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the bimodality analysis.

claim: In the case of motion direction, bimodality could largely explain the pattern of representational similarity between areas and measures.
source: Importantly, in the case of motion direction, bimodality could largely explain the pattern of representational similarity between areas and measures (R2 = 0.28, p=0).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the regression analysis.

claim: Small bimodality differences in color tuning did not affect representational similarity.
source: This was not the case for the small bimodality differences in color tuning, which did not affect representational similarity (R2 = 0, p=0.99).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the regression analysis.

claim: Similar motion direction bimodality led to V4 and IT showing similar motion representations, which were also similar to those in monkey EEG and human MEG.
source: Thus, similar motion direction bimodality led to V4 and IT showing similar motion representations, which were also similar to those in monkey EEG and human MEG.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the bimodality and RSA results.

claim: The presence of a bimodality effect in MEG, EEG, LFP, multi-unit and sorted unit data suggests that it was not caused by anisotropies in the large-scale organization of motion direction tuning, but rather by properties of individual units.
source: The presence of a bimodality effect in MEG, EEG, LFP, multi-unit and sorted unit data suggests that it was not caused by anisotropies in the large-scale organization of motion direction tuning, but rather by properties of individual units
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of bimodality across scales.

claim: Direction tuning curves in area V4 were bimodal.
source: Indeed, direction tuning curves in areas V4 (SUA: p=1*10−9, MUA: p=8*10−11, LFP: p=0.03) were bimodal
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support.

claim: Direction tuning curves in area MT were not bimodal.
source: whereas direction tuning curves in area MT (SUA: p=0.66, MUA: p=0.31, LFP: p=0.87) or color tuning curves in either area (all p>0.42) were not (Figure 7D and F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 7.

claim: Color tuning curves in V4 and MT were not bimodal.
source: whereas direction tuning curves in area MT (SUA: p=0.66, MUA: p=0.31, LFP: p=0.87) or color tuning curves in either area (all p>0.42) were not (Figure 7D and F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding with statistical support and reference to Figure 7.

claim: Information about motion direction and color was present in invasively recorded signals in many cortical areas in macaque monkeys as well as in non-invasive electrophysiological data from macaques and humans.
source: We found that information about motion direction and color was present in invasively recorded signals in many cortical areas in macaque monkeys as well as in non-invasive electrophysiological data from macaques and humans.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: Dissecting the information structure revealed representations according to perceptual similarity for color in all areas, and for motion direction in dorsal and frontal areas.
source: Dissecting the information structure revealed representations according to perceptual similarity for color in all areas, and for motion direction in dorsal and frontal areas.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: V4 and IT motion direction representations were bimodal, indicative of orientation rather than direction selectivity.
source: Contrary to that, V4 and IT motion direction representations were bimodal, indicative of orientation rather than direction selectivity.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings with an interpretation.

claim: The same bimodal pattern for motion direction was found in monkey EEG and human MEG, as confirmed by representational similarity analysis.
source: We found the same bimodal pattern in monkey EEG and human MEG, as confirmed by representational similarity analysis.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: Together with converging evidence from latency and information distributions, the results pointed to early visual and ventral stream areas such as V4 as the main drivers of EEG and MEG representations.
source: Together with converging evidence from latency and information distributions this pointed to early visual and ventral stream areas such as V4 as the main drivers of EEG and MEG representations
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Dorsal areas like MT did not appear to strongly contribute to non-invasive signals.
source: while dorsal areas like MT did not appear to strongly contribute to non-invasive signals.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Color and motion information was found in all areas measured, rather than in a small amount of specialized areas.
source: Consistent with earlier reports (An et al., 2012; Mendoza-Halliday et al., 2014; Siegel et al., 2015), we found color and motion information in all areas we measured, rather than in a small amount of specialized areas.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to earlier reports.

claim: The amount of information strongly depended on the area.
source: Nonetheless, the amount of information strongly depended on the area.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation.

claim: The motion direction decoding accuracies found were lower than previously reported in both area MT and prefrontal cortex.
source: Interestingly, the motion direction decoding accuracies we found were lower than previously reported in both area MT and prefrontal cortex (Mendoza-Halliday et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Mendoza-Halliday et al., 2014.

claim: Differences in decoding accuracy can be attributed to differences in the paradigm and analysis strategy.
source: This can largely be attributed to differences in the paradigm and analysis strategy
evidence: This is an inference about the reasons for observed differences.

claim: A clustering of both color and motion direction has been reported in several areas of the visual system.
source: Indeed, a clustering of both color (Conway and Tsao, 2009; Roe et al., 2012; Tanigawa et al., 2010) and motion direction (Albright et al., 1984; Li et al., 2013; Tanigawa et al., 2010) has been reported in several areas of the visual system.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Successful decoding of stimulus color and motion direction was not attributable to confounding factors, but likely stemmed from true feature-related signals.
source: This suggests that our successful decoding of stimulus color and motion direction was not attributable to confounding factors, but likely stemmed from true feature-related signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of clustering in the visual system.

claim: The results do not unequivocally identify the sources of visual information in MEG and EEG.
source: Crucially, even though we recorded invasively in many areas, our results do not unequivocally identify the sources of visual information in MEG and EEG.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the study.

claim: Neither color nor motion direction representations are limited to the areas recorded from.
source: First, neither color nor motion direction representations are limited to the areas we recorded from.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the study.

claim: Due to the simple feature spaces used for stimuli, many areas are expected to show highly similar tuning properties.
source: Secondly, partially due to the simple feature spaces used for our stimuli, many areas are expected to show highly similar tuning properties.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the study.

claim: Based on RSA, the non-invasively measured information stems from areas with tuning similar to V4 or IT.
source: Based on RSA, we can therefore only conclude that the non-invasively measured information stems from areas with tuning similar to V4 or IT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RSA results with acknowledgment of limitations.

claim: It is reasonable to assume that earlier visual areas strongly contributed to the non-invasive signals.
source: It is reasonable to assume that earlier visual areas strongly contributed to this
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the results.

claim: Source level searchlight analysis revealed strong information peaks in occipital cortex, corroborating the assumption that earlier visual areas contributed to non-invasive signals.
source: which is corroborated by our source level searchlight analysis revealing strong information peaks in occipital cortex.
evidence: This is a statement of supporting evidence for the previous claim.

claim: Area V1 exhibits a more bimodal motion direction tuning (i.e. orientation or axis tuning) than area MT.
source: Furthermore, it has been shown that for example area V1 exhibits a more bimodal motion direction tuning (i.e. orientation or axis tuning) than area MT (Albright, 1984)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Albright, 1984.

claim: The structure of color representations decodable from area V1 using fMRI is not in agreement with perceptual similarity.
source: There is, however, previous evidence that the structure of color representations decodable from area V1 using fMRI is not in agreement with perceptual similarity (Brouwer and Heeger, 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Brouwer and Heeger, 2013.

claim: In area MT, cortical columns with opposite preferred motion directions along the same axis lie spatially close to each other.
source: Notably, in area MT cortical columns with opposite preferred motion directions along the same axis lie spatially close to each other (Albright et al., 1984; Born and Bradley, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Albright et al., 1984 and Born and Bradley, 2005.

claim: The spatial organization of MT columns could, in principle, lead to a diminished decodability of opposite motion directions from mass signals such as EEG, MEG or fMRI.
source: This could, in principle, lead to a diminished decodability of opposite motion directions from mass signals such as EEG, MEG or fMRI.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a possible mechanism.

claim: Motion direction has been successfully decoded from BOLD signals in area MT.
source: While several recent fMRI studies have focused on motion axis decoding (Schneider et al., 2019; Zimmermann et al., 2011), motion direction has been successfully decoded from BOLD signals in area MT (Kamitani and Tong, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to relevant fMRI studies.

claim: Given that motion representations are prevalent across visual cortex, it is unlikely that MT was a dominant source of the bimodally tuned motion signals measured in EEG and MEG.
source: Given that motion representations are prevalent across visual cortex (An et al., 2012), we consider it unlikely that MT was a dominant source of the bimodally tuned motion signals we measured in EEG and MEG.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the evidence, supported by a citation.

claim: The information decoded from non-invasive signals originated in a mixture of several early visual areas.
source: In sum, this suggests that the information decoded from non-invasive signals originated in a mixture of several early visual areas.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the discussion.

claim: Recordings from additional visual areas using the same paradigm are required to further clarify the sources of non-invasive signals.
source: Recordings from additional visual areas using the same paradigm are required to further clarify this.
evidence: This is a statement about future work needed.

claim: High electrode density and methods identical to those used in human M/EEG enabled source reconstruction and direct relation of measures across species.
source: High electrode density and methods identical to those used in human M/EEG enabled us to perform source reconstruction and directly relate measures across species.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological advantages of the approach.

claim: Previous studies measuring EEG in nonhuman primates were typically restricted to only a few electrodes.
source: The few available previous studies measuring EEG in nonhuman primates were typically restricted to only a few electrodes (Bimbi et al., 2018; Snyder et al., 2015; Snyder et al., 2018) and used diverging methods such as skull-screw electrodes, or both (Godlove et al., 2011; Musall et al., 2014; Reinhart et al., 2012; Whittingstall and Logothetis, 2009; Woodman et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Monkey EEG can serve as a missing link to enable the disentangling of species differences from differences in measurement modality.
source: We show how monkey EEG can serve as a missing link to enable the disentangling of species differences from differences in measurement modality.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of the approach.

claim: Finding bimodal motion direction tuning in monkey EEG allowed inference that it was not due to a decreased influence of MT-like areas in the human, but rather a sign of a general dominance of V4-like tuning in non-invasive signals.
source: Finding the same result in monkey EEG allowed us to infer that it was not due to a decreased influence of MT-like areas in the human, but rather a sign of a general dominance of V4-like tuning in non-invasive signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the monkey EEG results.

claim: When applied in addition to ongoing invasive experiments, the marginal cost of monkey EEG is comparably small.
source: When applied in addition to ongoing invasive experiments, the marginal cost of monkey EEG is comparably small.
evidence: This is a statement about the practical advantages of the approach.

claim: Monkey EEG is non-invasive, depends mostly on standard human neuroscience tools, and does not necessitate further animal training.
source: It is non-invasive, depends mostly on standard human neuroscience tools, and does not necessitate further animal training.
evidence: This is a statement about the practical advantages of the approach.

claim: Another possibility to achieve the goal of linking invasive and non-invasive electrophysiology is given by invasive electrophysiological recordings in human patients, which are severely constrained by the requirement for medical necessity.
source: Notably, another possibility to achieve this goal is given by invasive electrophysiological recordings in human patients, that are however severely constrained by the requirement for medical necessity.
evidence: This is a statement about an alternative approach and its limitations.

claim: Information-based analyses are powerful tools to relate very different signals based on their information contents.
source: Such analyses are powerful tools to relate very different signals based on their information contents.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of the analytical approach.

claim: Information-based analyses may include data from different measurement techniques, such as MEG and fMRI, or species.
source: This may not only include data from different measurement techniques, such as MEG and fMRI (Cichy et al., 2014; Cichy et al., 2016a), or species (Cichy et al., 2014; Kriegeskorte et al., 2008b)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: Information-based analyses may also include cognitive or computational models.
source: but also cognitive or computational models (Cichy et al., 2016b; Wardle et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: The same framework can be applied to complex task conditions instead of comparing representations of simple sensory stimuli.
source: Furthermore, instead of comparing representations of simple sensory stimuli, the same framework can be applied to complex task conditions (Hebart et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hebart et al., 2018.

claim: The framework of cross-species and cross-scale comparisons is not limited to information-based analyses.
source: We would like to highlight that our framework of cross-species and cross-scale comparisons is not limited to information-based analyses.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader applicability of the approach.

claim: It will be highly interesting to compare and pinpoint specific spectral signatures of circuit activity in signals on all scales.
source: For example we anticipate that it will be highly interesting to compare and pinpoint specific spectral signatures of circuit activity in signals on all scales (Donner and Siegel, 2011; Siegel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future work, supported by citations.

claim: Comparing spectral signatures has been successful in some cases.
source: This has been successful in some cases (Sherman et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: The large scale approach could significantly benefit the comparison of spectral signatures to gain further specificity.
source: but could significantly benefit from the present large scale approach to gain further specificity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the value of the approach.

claim: With sufficient knowledge about mechanistic signatures on all scales, this could facilitate the establishment of transfer functions between circuit activity and non-invasive human electrophysiology.
source: In the long term, with sufficient knowledge about mechanistic signatures on all scales, this could facilitate the establishment of transfer functions between circuit activity and non-invasive human electrophysiology (Cohen, 2017; Donner and Siegel, 2011; Siegel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future possibilities, supported by citations.

claim: Macro-scale signals alone always suffer from an ill-posed inverse problem when trying to infer micro-scale properties.
source: As has been noted before (Sprague et al., 2018), macro-scale signals alone always suffer from an ill-posed inverse problem when trying to infer micro-scale properties.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sprague et al., 2018.

claim: The approach of dense recordings on all scales allows bridging the gap of the inverse problem by constraining inferences.
source: The approach of dense recordings on all scales, as outlined here, allows to bridge this gap by constraining inferences.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of the approach.

claim: Such developments would allow quick and inexpensive access to circuit function in the human brain, both for basic research and in clinical practice.
source: Such developments would allow quick and inexpensive access to circuit function in the human brain, both for basic research and in clinical practice (Siegel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future possibilities, supported by a citation.

claim: Color and motion direction can be decoded from non-invasive electrophysiology in humans and monkeys.
source: In sum, we show that color and motion direction can be decoded from non-invasive electrophysiology in humans and monkeys.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: Simple stimulus representations are dominated by signals from early ventral stream areas.
source: Our results suggest that such simple stimulus representations are dominated by signals from early ventral stream areas.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the results.

claim: This inference serves as a proof-of-principle for using high-density monkey EEG as a bridge technology to link scales and species.
source: This inference serves as a proof-of-principle for, and was enabled by, using high-density monkey EEG as a bridge technology to link scales and species.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the value of the approach.

claim: Microelectrode recordings were performed in two adult rhesus macaques, one male (monkey R) and one female (monkey P).
source: Microelectrode recordings were performed in two adult rhesus macaques, one male (monkey R) and one female (monkey P).
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental subjects.

claim: Each monkey was implanted with a titanium headpost to immobilize the head.
source: Each monkey was implanted with a titanium headpost to immobilize the head.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: Three titanium recording chambers were stereotactically implanted over frontal, parietal, and occipitotemporal cortices in the left hemisphere.
source: Following behavioral training, three titanium recording chambers were stereotactically implanted over frontal, parietal, and occipitotemporal cortices in the left hemisphere.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: All procedures followed the guidelines of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Committee on Animal Care and the National Institutes of Health.
source: All procedures followed the guidelines of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Committee on Animal Care and the National Institutes of Health.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: Colors were sampled from a circle in CIEL*C*h color space such that they had equal luminance and saturation.
source: We sampled dot colors from a circle in CIEL*C*h color space such that they had equal luminance and saturation.
evidence: This is a direct description of the stimulus generation method.

claim: The background color was always a uniform black.
source: The background color was always a uniform black.
evidence: This is a direct description of the stimulus properties.

claim: Individual stimuli contained both luminance and chromaticity contrasts between background and dots.
source: Therefore, individual stimuli contained both luminance and chromaticity contrasts between background and dots
evidence: This is a direct description of the stimulus properties.

claim: The only features varying over stimuli were color hue and motion direction.
source: whereas the only features varying over stimuli were color hue and motion direction.
evidence: This is a direct description of the stimulus properties.

claim: Microelectrode activity was recorded in a total of 71 recording sessions, 47 in monkey P and 24 in monkey R.
source: Microelectrode activity was recorded in a total of 71 recording sessions, 47 in monkey P and 24 in monkey R.
evidence: This is a direct description of the data collection.

claim: Combined over all sessions of both monkeys, 58,056 stimuli were presented.
source: Combined over all sessions of both monkeys, 58,056 stimuli were presented.
evidence: This is a direct description of the data collection.

claim: Epoxy-coated tungsten electrodes were acutely lowered in up to six areas out of the lateral prefrontal cortex, frontal eye fields (FEF), lateral intraparietal cortex (LIP), inferotemporal cortex (TEO), visual area V4, and the middle temporal area (MT).
source: In each recording session, we acutely lowered Epoxy-coated tungsten electrodes in up to six areas out of the lateral prefrontal cortex, frontal eye fields (FEF), lateral intraparietal cortex (LIP), inferotemporal cortex (TEO), visual area V4, and the middle temporal area (MT).
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: Neuronal activity was recorded across a maximum of 108 electrodes simultaneously.
source: Neuronal activity was recorded across a maximum of 108 electrodes simultaneously.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: All signals were recorded broad-band at 40 kHz referenced to the titanium headpost.
source: All signals were recorded broad-band at 40 kHz referenced to the titanium headpost.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: Data were analyzed from a total of 4505 cortical recording sites.
source: We analyzed data from a total of 4505 cortical recording sites (V4: 372, IT: 148, MT: 272, LIP: 897, FEF: 1067, PFC: 1749).
evidence: This is a direct description of the data analyzed.

claim: Scalp EEG was measured in two male adult rhesus monkeys.
source: We measured scalp EEG in two male adult rhesus monkeys.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental subjects.

claim: All procedures for monkey EEG were approved by local authorities (Regierungspräsidium Tübingen).
source: All procedures were approved by local authorities (Regierungspräsidium Tübingen).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: EEG was recorded using 65 Ag/AgCl electrodes and a NeurOne recording system in 11 recording sessions.
source: EEG was recorded using 65 Ag/AgCl electrodes and a NeurOne recording system (Bittium, Oulu, Finland) in 11 recording sessions
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: During monkey EEG recordings, a total of 167,762 stimuli were presented.
source: during which a total of 167,762 stimuli were presented.
evidence: This is a direct description of the data collection.

claim: All channels were referenced to a central electrode, recorded with a sampling rate of 5 kHz and low-pass filtered online at 1250 Hz.
source: All channels were referenced to a central electrode, recorded with a sampling rate of 5 kHz and low-pass filtered online at 1250 Hz.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: Electrodes were placed on the scalp using a custom-built 66-channel EEG cap covering the entire scalp.
source: Electrodes were placed on the scalp using a custom-built 66-channel EEG cap (Easycap, Herrsching, Germany) covering the entire scalp.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: EEG caps were fabricated to match the individual animal's head shape based on anatomical MRIs and 3D-printed head models.
source: Based on anatomical MRIs and 3D-printed head models, EEG caps were fabricated to match the individual animal's head shape.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: 11 healthy volunteers (three female, 28.6 + −4.8 years) with normal or corrected-to-normal vision participated in the human MEG study.
source: 11 healthy volunteers (three female, 28.6 + −4.8 years) with normal or corrected-to-normal vision participated in this study.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental subjects.

claim: The human MEG study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the ethics committee of the University of Tübingen.
source: The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the ethics committee of the University of Tübingen.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: All human participants gave written informed consent before participating.
source: All participants gave written informed consent before participating.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: MEG was recorded with 275 channels at a sampling rate of 2,343.75 Hz in a magnetically shielded chamber.
source: We recorded MEG (Omega 2000, CTF Systems, Inc, Port Coquitlam, Canada) with 275 channels at a sampling rate of 2,343.75 Hz in a magnetically shielded chamber.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental methods.

claim: The eleven human participants completed one recording session each, resulting in a total of 237,348 stimuli being presented.
source: The eleven participants completed one recording session each, resulting in a total of 237,348 stimuli being presented.
evidence: This is a direct description of the data collection.

claim: Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) was used to extract the content and structure of information about stimulus features from all signal types.
source: We used linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to extract the content and structure of information about stimulus features from all signal types.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: For EEG and MEG, the analysis was repeated in a 10-fold cross-validation scheme for each session.
source: For EEG and MEG, we repeated this analysis in a 10-fold cross-validation scheme for each session, using all available sensors.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: For SUA, MUA and LFP, 2-fold instead of 10-fold cross-validation was used.
source: For SUA, MUA and LFP, we used 2-fold instead of 10-fold cross-validation.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: A cluster sign permutation procedure was used to assess the presence of significant information.
source: We assessed the presence of significant information using a cluster sign permutation procedure (similar to Cichy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods, with a citation.

claim: Information latency was computed as the time point classifier performance reached half its peak.
source: Information latency was computed as the time point classifier performance reached half its peak.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: A control experiment was performed in one human participant to control for possible effects of luminance on color classification.
source: To control for possible effects of luminance on color classification, we measured MEG as described above in one human participant during an additional control experiment.
evidence: This is a direct description of a control experiment.

claim: A psychophysical control experiment was performed in a third macaque monkey to assess if stimuli were perceptually equiluminant to macaque monkeys.
source: As color vision in macaques and humans is slightly different, we performed a psychophysical control experiment in a third macaque monkey to assess if our stimuli were in fact perceptually equiluminant to macaque monkeys.
evidence: This is a direct description of a control experiment.

claim: An adapted minimum motion technique using eye-movements as a readout was used in the macaque equiluminance control experiment.
source: To this end, we used an adapted minimum motion technique using eye-movements as a readout (Logothetis and Charles, 1990).
evidence: This is a direct description of the control experiment methods, with a citation.

claim: Equiluminant colors generated in L*C*h-space were also close to perceptually equiluminant for the macaque monkey used in the psychophysical control experiment.
source: Using a minimum-motion technique and eye movements as readout (Logothetis and Charles, 1990), we found that equiluminant colors generated in L*C*h-space were also close to perceptually equiluminant for this monkey (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the control experiment, with reference to a figure.

claim: Simultaneous MEG and EEG data were acquired in one of the human participants to assess whether the inverted relationship between color and motion information in monkeys and humans was due to differences between EEG and MEG.
source: To assess whether the inverted relationship between color and motion information in monkeys and humans was due to differences between EEG and MEG, we simultaneously measured EEG and MEG in one of the eleven human participants.
evidence: This is a direct description of a control experiment.

claim: Source reconstruction was performed on monkey EEG and human MEG data to assess the distribution of information in human and macaque brains.
source: To assess the distribution of information in human and macaque brains, we performed source reconstruction on monkey EEG and human MEG data and repeated the multivariate classification in a searchlight fashion.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: Structural MRI scans were used to create individual realistic head models for source reconstruction.
source: We used structural MRI scans to create individual realistic head models.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: Single-shell head models were generated for MEG source reconstruction.
source: For MEG source reconstruction, we generated single-shell head models (Nolte, 2003).
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods, with a citation.

claim: Detailed finite element head models were generated for EEG source reconstruction using the SimBio toolbox.
source: These overall six tissue types (WM, GM, CSF, skull, scalp, titanium) were then used to generate detailed finite element head models (FEM) using the SimBio toolbox (Fingberg et al., 2003) as implemented in Fieldtrip.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods, with a citation.

claim: Representational similarity analysis was used to compare representational structure between brain areas, measurement methods and species.
source: We compared representational structure between brain areas, measurement methods and species using representational similarity analysis.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: The temporal average of the confusion matrices was computed over a time period in which stimulus information was available (50–250 ms).
source: To this end, we computed the temporal average of the confusion matrices over a time period in which stimulus information was available (50–250 ms).
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: A permutation procedure was used to assess significant similarity in RSA.
source: To assess significant similarity, we used a permutation procedure in which we randomly reassigned stimulus labels to the rows and columns of the confusion matrices 10,000 times.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: Population tuning bimodality was quantified by calculating the slope in prediction probability between opposite and next-to-opposite stimuli normalized by the range of prediction probabilities.
source: We quantified the presence of such bimodal tuning across areas and measurement scales by calculating the slope in prediction probability between opposite (180-degree difference) and next-to-opposite (135- and 225-degree difference) stimuli, normalized by the range of prediction probabilities (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods, with reference to Figure 7.

claim: Linear regression was used to estimate the contribution of bimodality differences to the pattern of similarity between invasively measured areas and signal types.
source: We used linear regression to estimate the contribution of bimodality differences to the pattern of similarity between invasively measured areas and signal types (Figure 7C and E).
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods, with reference to Figure 7.

claim: One-way ANOVAs were performed on each channel to select those containing information about color or motion direction.
source: To estimate average tuning curves of single units, multi-units and LFP channels in each cortical area, we performed one-way ANOVAs on each channel to select those containing information about color or motion direction, respectively, with a statistical threshold of p<0.05.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis methods.

claim: All analyses were performed in MATLAB, using custom code as well as the Fieldtrip and SPM toolboxes.
source: All analyses were performed in MATLAB, using custom code as well as the Fieldtrip (Oostenveld et al., 2011) and SPM toolboxes.
evidence: This is a direct description of the analysis software, with a citation.
